newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, seen in flat trend.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, seen in flat trend.

text.p: Polish shares extended Monday's fall but analysts said a general lack of signals suggested the market would remain in its horizontal trend already nearly a month long.
But they were divided on whether there was a greater chance for slight gains or slight growth before year-end.
Some analysts said recent gains by large-cap stocks foreshadowed overall market growth.
"Some big stocks held their own today...which suggests large investors are inclined to buy at current prices," said Tomasz Berent, an analyst at IB Austria Securities.

Large-cap BPH, Zywiec and Gorazdze were among the top gainers, each rising 2.3, 2.2 and 2.1 percent, while other heavyweights such Stomil Olsztyn and Rolimpex, which fell 2.8 and 0.8 percent, showed strong buying after price fixing.
The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.6 percent to 13,568.4 points and turnover eased 4.9 percent to 85.5 million zlotys on both markets.
Analysts expecting a slight fall this month said a bad sign was the greater number of firms that fell on Tuesday relative to Monday despite the lower overall market drop.
Pessimists also pointed to likely low turnovers before the Christmas holiday at the end of the month.
Analysts said relatively low turnovers suggested the moves of biggest loser Kety, down seven percent, and top gainer Bytom, up 5.3 percent, were exaggerated.
Continuous tradeturnover was at 2.4 million zlotys with three stocks closing higher and four flat.
NFI units fell 3.1 percent to 140.5 zlotys in 9.9-million-zloty trade in the regular bourse session and fell 1.8 percent to 139 million zlotys in 18.8-million-zloty continuous trade.
